citation.note: Notice of payday changes: If an employer alters regular paydays, 30 days' written notice must be given to each employee before the change takes effect (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 48-1230).
Paid sick leave 1hr/30hrs after 80 hours worked, 11+-employee threshold; 40hr/yr small-employer and 56hr/yr larger-employer caps; carryover or payout-and-refresh; eff. 2025-10-01 (Initiative 436).

body.interaction_rule: Accrued paid sick time preserved on promotion or base-pay change; accrual continues at 1 hour per 30 hours worked (Initiative 436).

citation.note: Pay Frequency: No state law mandates a specific pay frequency (weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly, monthly).
Unpaid wages including accrued vacation/PTO due on separation; next regular payday or within 2 weeks, whichever sooner; accrued PTO counts as wages (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 48-1230).

body.deadline_description: Unpaid wages including accrued vacation/PTO due on separation; next regular payday or within 2 weeks, whichever sooner; accrued PTO counts as wages (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 48-1230).

citation.note: Nebraska WARN Act (LB 921) requires 90-day notice for mass layoffs of 25+ employees: State mini-WARN applies to separations of 25 or more employees on the same day, for the same reason, expected to last 7+ days; federal 60-day/100-employee WARN applies alongside.

body.note: Nebraska WARN Act (LB 921) requires 90-day notice for mass layoffs of 25+ employees: State mini-WARN applies to separations of 25 or more employees on the same day, for the same reason, expected to last 7+ days; federal 60-day/100-employee WARN applies alongside.

citation.note: Minimum wage: $15/hour (2026), with annual increases: Effective January 1, 2026, minimum wage is $15/hour per Initiative 433 (LB 258); increases 1.75% annually starting January 1, 2027, calculated and published by October 15 each year.
Sex-based wage discrimination barred for equal work requiring equal skill, effort, and responsibility under similar conditions; document classifications and conditions (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 48-1219).
Wage statement each regular payday showing employer identity, hours paid, wages earned, and deductions (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 48-1230).
Wage-disclosure retaliation barred (§ 48-1114); retaliation for invoking Equal Pay Act rights barred (§ 48-1221).

citation.note: Retain separation documentation: Maintain final-pay records, separation notices, and related documentation.
Drug and alcohol testing neither required nor prohibited; no Nebraska-specific procedures, timing, or notice mandates (§§ 48-1901 to 48-1910).
Breach notification as soon as possible and without unreasonable delay; law-enforcement delay only if investigation impeded (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 87-803).
